senses.definition: Senses referring to subjective quality.

examples: The tree frog that they encountered was truly a fine specimen.

quotes.text: "A fine man, that Dunwody, yonder," commented the young captain, as they parted, and as he turned to his prisoner. "We'll see him on in Washington some day. He is strengthening his forces now against Mr. Benton out there.[…]."

subsenses.definition: (informal) Being acceptable, adequate, passable, or satisfactory.
examples: How are you today? – Fine.
Will this one do? It's got a dent in it. – Yeah, it'll be fine, I guess.
It's fine with me if you stay out late, so long as you're back by three.

quotes.text: On the surface, everything is fine. The sleek, futuristic spaceship setting is fine (if a little cold), the acting is fine (or better than fine, in Lawrence’s case), the music is fine, the lighting is fine, the editing, the camerawork—all fine.

quotes.text: Now all this was very fine, but not at all in keeping with the Celebrity's character as I had come to conceive it. The idea that adulation ever cloyed on him was ludicrous in itself. In fact I thought the whole story fishy, and came very near to saying so.

examples: That man is so fine that I'd jump into his pants without a moment's hesitation.

subsenses.definition: An answer often used to cover an unnecessary explanation, rather to avoid conflict or an argument. Saying "I'm fine" can be used to avoid inquiry when the speaker is not really okay.
examples: Do you want to talk about what happened? – [sharply, with annoyance or discomfort] I'm fine!

senses.definition: Senses referring to objective quality.

subsenses.definition: Of a particular grade of quality, usually between very good and very fine, and below mint.
examples: The small scratch meant that his copy of “X-Men #2” was merely fine when it otherwise would have been “near mint”.

quotes.text: If the afternoon was fine they strolled together in the park, very slowly, and with pauses to draw breath wherever the ground sloped upward. The slightest effort made the patient cough.
quotes.reference: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter XXIII, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:

subsenses.definition: Consisting of especially minute particulates; made up of particularly small pieces.
examples: Grind it into a fine powder.
When she touched the artifact, it collapsed into a heap of fine dust.

quotes.text: And if thy oblation be a meate offering baken in the frying pan,it ſhalbe made of fine flowꝛe with oyle.
quotes.reference: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Leviticus 2:7:

subsenses.definition: Particularly slender; especially thin, narrow, or of small girth.
examples: The threads were so fine that you had to look through a magnifying glass to see them.

quotes.text: But as our urban lives have grown more pressed for time, we have diced our opportunity costs finer and finer; from budgeting days or slabs of hours, we have come to rationing minutes.

subsenses.definition: Made of slender or thin filaments.
examples: They protected themselves from the small parasites with a fine wire mesh.

subsenses.definition: Having a (specified) proportion of pure metal in its composition.
examples: Coins nine tenths fine.

senses.definition: (cricket) Behind the batsman and at a small angle to the line between the wickets.
examples: […]to nudge it through the covers (or tickle it down to fine leg) for a four[…]

senses.definition: (obsolete) Subtle; thin; tenuous.

quotes.text: The eye standeth in the finer medium and the object in the grosser.

senses.definition: Well, nicely, in a positive, agreeable way.
examples: Everything worked out fine.

senses.definition: (dated, dialect, colloquial) Finely; elegantly; delicately.
(pool, billiards) In a manner so that the driven ball strikes the object ball so far to one side as to be barely deflected, the object ball being driven to one side.
Expression of (typically) reluctant or agreement.
Expression of (typically) reluctant acceptance, without further argument or discussion, of another person's viewpoint.
Fine champagne; French brandy.

examples: They filtered silt and fines out of the soil.

senses.definition: A fee levied as punishment for breaking the law.
examples: The fine for jay-walking has gone from two dollars to thirty in the last fifteen years.
